title: Chicago cabarets and bands of the early 1920s
summary: Recalls the many Chicago places and bands: the Sunset, the Plantation, the Entertainers, the Deluxe, the Vendome, with Dutrey and Noone in various bands.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: If you don't, it's all right. So the musicians just had a ball, especially as young musicians. We had so many places to go. The entertainers was open. We had Wic- Memories are awful bad now.
It was a company, wasn't it? John Wycliffe.

Yeah, John Wycliffe had the band entertainers. And the Deluxe and the Dreamin' was open. Then you had Jimmy Loom and the Vendome was going big. And Louie was doubling. Later on, before Louie came back, then he doubled from the Vendome. The Vendome to the Sunset. That's when Natty Dominic was playing there with him, you understand? And Dutre. All those bands split up and the men just went like the Four Wings. Dutre was over there with Carol Dixon's band. So I may be in some instances, I may be a little ahead of myself, but I try to rectify

But I think I was very fortunate in being around during this time, and I think I was very fortunate during this time, and even before that. In New Orleans I remember Joe Oliver. I was going to ask a bit more.
